title: Therapeutic Potential of Polydatin Against Cancer Cachexia by Regulating the STAT3 Signaling Pathway.
authors: Ho, Phuong T; Kang, Nalae; Luong, Quynh Xuan Thi; Hakim, Meutia Diva; Kawalin, Kantawong; Heo, Soo-Jin; Kang, Hee; Lee, Taek Kyun; Lee, Sukchan
one_liner_zh: 该文研究虎杖苷通过STAT3信号通路改善癌症恶病质，仅含分子对接分析小分子与STAT3通路蛋白的相互作用，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Background/Objectives: Cancer cachexia is a wasting syndrome with significant loss of body weight and muscle mass caused by inflammation and abnormal metabolism in advanced cancers. Despite its detrimental effects on patients, no standard treatment has been established for this syndrome. Thus, finding new treatments will broaden the remedy for cancer cachexia, resulting in increased survival in patients with terminal cancer. Methods: In this study, we assessed the therapeutic effects of the natural compound polydatin on cancer cachexia in vitro and in vivo using C2C12 myoblasts and CT26-bearing mice to elucidate the mechanisms of how it ameliorates muscle atrophy. At the same time, molecular docking analysis of polydatin with the IL6/STAT3 signaling pathway was conducted to demonstrate their interaction. Results: Our data showed that polydatin treatment at 100 mg/kg could attenuate symptoms of cancer cachexia including body weight loss, muscle strength and severe inflammation. Muscle mass reduction-with the shrinking of muscle fibers, an increase in the expression levels of two E3 ubiquitin ligases (MuRF1 and Atrogin-1) and interleukin-6, and a downregulation of MyHC-observed in CT26-bearing mice was reversed by polydatin at 100 mg/kg. On C2C12 myotubes, polydatin also ameliorated muscle atrophy induced by the CT26 conditioned medium and suppressed STAT3 phosphorylation at the concentration of 200 microM. Structural features of polydatin in the proteins in the STAT3 pathway were identified through molecular docking simulations. Conclusions: Taken together, polydatin significantly attenuated muscle atrophy in a cancer cachexia model by inhibiting the STAT3 signaling pathway; thus, it might be a promising compound in the development of drug candidates for cancer cachexia therapy.
abstract_zh: 背景/目的：癌症恶病质是一种消耗性综合征，以晚期癌症中由炎症和异常代谢引起的显著体重下降和肌肉质量损失为特征。尽管其对患者有不利影响，但目前尚无针对该综合征的标准治疗方法。因此，寻找新疗法将拓宽癌症恶病质的治疗手段，从而提高终末期癌症患者的生存率。方法：在本研究中，我们评估了天然化合物虎杖苷 (polydatin) 对癌症恶病质的治疗作用，通过体外和体内实验，使用C2C12成肌细胞和携带CT26肿瘤的小鼠，以阐明其改善肌肉萎缩的机制。同时，对虎杖苷与IL6/STAT3信号通路进行了分子对接 (molecular docking) 分析，以证明它们之间的相互作用。结果：我们的数据显示，虎杖苷以100 mg/kg剂量治疗可减轻癌症恶病质的症状，包括体重下降、肌肉力量和严重炎症。在携带CT26肿瘤的小鼠中观察到的肌肉质量减少——伴随肌纤维收缩、两种E3泛素连接酶（MuRF1和Atrogin-1）及白细胞介素-6表达水平升高，以及MyHC下调——被100 mg/kg虎杖苷逆转。在C2C12肌管上，虎杖苷也改善了由CT26条件培养基诱导的肌肉萎缩，并在200微摩尔浓度下抑制了STAT3磷酸化。通过分子对接模拟，鉴定了虎杖苷在STAT3通路蛋白中的结构特征。结论：综合来看，虎杖苷通过抑制STAT3信号通路显著减轻了癌症恶病质模型中的肌肉萎缩；因此，它可能是在开发癌症恶病质治疗药物候选物中的一个有前景的化合物。
